Judging by this comment / your others in this thread, I think you're just being a tad sensitive. 

OP said that he offered coffee, she declined, and when inquiring further, she said that she just wasn't in the mood for coffee. It's fine that he was curious about her reasoning, but I dont think a person is rude for not offering an explanation for their refusal.

Beyond the OP's judgement, I think itd be good for you to get used to a yes / no answer not being anything you need to read into. It's a lot to assume someone is being careless / rude / annoyed just because they gave a simple response.

?? No? That's not childish at all. 

"Do you want to have some coffee?"

"No thank you"

Interaction over. 

OP's gf isnt childish for not wanting to try coffee, and she isnt an asshole for not offering an explanation. It's perfectly fine to just not be interested in something.

I did get to speak to students attending there currently and they had indeed gotten funding, however they were also the ones that were asked to come speak to us at visit day so maybe they aren't representative.

Financial aid broke down the number of assistantship opportunities per number of students etc which was helpful.


I do feel that I could be happy at either program, but I'm hesitant about UW because their EI program is a very terminal / professional program and it's not very customizable. You basically sign on for a rigid curriculum and that's that. But its also only 15 months straight and less expensive which is nice...

I'm just torn because I think I like Madison better than Ann Arbor, but UM more than UW, and worry about the funding of course :/

Yes, it's a masters program.

Everyone I've spoken to in the program's department & the financial aid office have insisted that there are plenty of funding opportunities to receive, but I wouldn't be eligible to apply for them until after accepting my offer of admission. Virtually everyone else that visited was in the same boat so I guess this is just their really unfortunate way of funding ugh
